subject: Civil Engineering
title: The 2010 Haiti vs. Chile Earthquakes
description: A fast breakdown of The 2010 Haiti vs. Chile Earthquakes for builders.

hook.text: Haiti — magnitude 7.0, 316,000 dead. Chile — magnitude 8.8, 525 dead. Why the difference?

buildup.text: Haiti had no seismic building code. Buildings were unreinforced masonry — they pancaked.

discovery.text: Chile enforces strict seismic codes. Reinforced concrete and steel frames held up.

twist.text: Chile's earthquake released 500 times more energy — yet killed 600 times fewer people.

climax.text: Building codes, enforcement, and engineering capacity determine who survives.

punchline.text: Earthquakes are natural. Disasters are man-made. Codes save lives.

quiz.question: Why did Haiti suffer far more casualties than Chile despite a weaker earthquake?
options: Haiti's earthquake struck at night when people were sleeping
Haiti lacked seismic building codes — unreinforced buildings collapsed catastrophically
Chile's earthquake occurred in a sparsely populated rural region

details.summary: The 2010 Haiti earthquake (magnitude 7.0) killed over 200,000 people while the far more powerful 2010 Chile earthquake (magnitude 8.8, 500 times more energy) killed 525 people.
details.whyItMatters: The Haiti-Chile comparison is the most powerful modern illustration that earthquakes do not kill people, but buildings do. Investment in seismic engineering and code enforcement saves orders of magnitude more lives than emergency response.
takeaways: Chile's magnitude 8.8 quake released 500 times more energy than Haiti's 7.0 quake
Haiti lost over 200,000 lives versus Chile's 525 despite far less energy released
Chile's enforced seismic building codes were the decisive difference in survival

faq.question: Why did the weaker Haiti earthquake kill hundreds of times more people than Chile's?
faq.answer: Haiti had no enforced building code, widespread unreinforced concrete block construction, no seismic detailing, and extreme poverty that prevented resilient building practices.

faq.question: What lessons from the Haiti-Chile comparison can be applied elsewhere?
faq.answer: Investing in seismic building codes and their enforcement is the single most effective earthquake preparation. Economic development that enables quality construction saves lives. Training construction workers in seismic detailing is crucial where informal building is common.
